requirements.text: Each candidate is an unperforated 100 mm long, 2 mm thick rectangular plate with its declared 40 mm or 60 mm width, within the 65 mm width envelope.

requirements.text: The numerical model fixes the complete X=0 face at 25 °C, applies total 4 W uniformly to the complete X=100 mm face, and insulates all four longitudinal faces.
The model uses constant thermal conductivity 200 W/(m·K); density 2700 kg/m³ is used only for comparative mass and is not presented as certified alloy data.
Both width candidates retain actual coarse and refined numerical temperature fields distinct from the analytical calculation and the input diagram.
Each numerical hot-end temperature rise agrees within 2% of Q·L/(k·W·t) using that candidate's declared dimensions and inputs.
sources: Geometry and boundary definitions; Reporting policy

requirements.text: Each refined candidate field has total heat removal within 1% of the declared 4 W input.
Each candidate's coarse-to-refined hot-end temperature-rise change is at most 2% and retains both mesh identities.
The 40 mm candidate exceeds the inclusive 45 °C hot-end limit under the declared model.
The 60 mm candidate is at or below the inclusive 45 °C hot-end limit under the declared model.
The sizing decision selects revision_60 as the narrowest declared candidate satisfying the inclusive 45 °C limit.
The output set contains candidate STEP geometry, numerical fields, heat-balance data, mesh/refinement evidence, and a machine-readable sizing decision with rationale.

requirements.text: Each candidate is an unperforated 120 mm long, 2 mm thick rectangular plate with declared width 60, 80, or 100 mm, within the 125 mm by 104 mm envelope.
The numerical model applies total 18 W uniformly to the complete X=120 mm face, uses a 35 °C external rail reference, and insulates all longitudinal faces.

Every required candidate includes the declared 0.15 K/W total whole-interface cold-end resistance using a mathematically equivalent candidate-specific boundary conversion; it is never treated as 0.15 m²·K/W or silently removed.
The model uses constant thermal conductivity 385 W/(m·K) and density 8960 kg/m³ as synthetic copper-like properties without claiming a certified grade.
All three required contact-resistance candidates retain actual coarse and refined numerical temperature fields distinct from analytical or ideal-contact comparisons.
sources: Contact-resistance requirement; Evidence, review, and limits

requirements.text: If the backend cannot represent total contact resistance, the result explicitly blocks that requirement and labels any ideal-contact solve as a separate noncompliant comparison.
Each required numerical hot-end temperature agrees within 2% of the rise predicted by 18 W times [L/(k·W·t)+0.15 K/W] for that candidate.
Each refined candidate field has total heat removal within 1% of the declared 18 W input.
Each candidate's coarse-to-refined hot-end temperature-rise change is at most 2% and retains both mesh identities.
The decision records the computed compliance outcome for 60, 80, and 100 mm widths against the inclusive 75 °C limit with the contact resistance included.
The sizing decision selects copper_80 as the lowest-mass declared candidate at or below 75 °C under the required resistance model.
A recorded design review confirms contact-resistance units, per-candidate interface area, material constants, and boundary names before solving.
The output set contains all candidate CAD, numerical fields, heat-balance data, coarse/fine mesh evidence, and a machine-readable sizing decision.
Reported conclusions remain limited to the synthetic passive link model and do not claim real lamp, rail, surface-temperature, cooling-system, hardware, or standards performance.
sources: Application and model boundary; Evidence, review, and limits

requirements.text: H1 bushing-seat center X is 30.00 ±0.20 mm in the lower-left workpiece top-face datum.
H1 bushing-seat center Y is 30.00 ±0.20 mm in the lower-left workpiece top-face datum.

Both flange pockets are 14.30 mm nominal diameter and 2.0 mm deep, support the flange from above, and leave the guide body unobstructed.
The 12 mm plate and 12 mm bushing body stackup is reported without silently shortening the bushing or claiming a press fit.
The jig registers on the workpiece left end and lower long edge with datum fences extending no more than 8 mm down the sides and 0.30 mm nominal clearance at the opposite non-datum edge.
Jig material does not intersect either complete CLAMP_LEFT or CLAMP_RIGHT occupied volume.
A clear +X arrow and DATUM LEFT text appear in a noncritical exterior region without intersecting bushing seats.

The digital result does not claim physical fit, guidance accuracy, clamp safety, standards compliance, machine commands, or production dispatch.

Every bushing uses a 12.15 mm body hole and an 18.30 mm diameter by 2.50 mm deep top counterbore with the flange bearing downward.
The 15.00 mm body spans the remaining bridge thickness and no secondary retainer or straight-sleeve substitution is asserted.

requirements.text: No jig material occupies X=65..115 mm, Y=15..65 mm in the declared chip-removal region, and the workpiece is not cut there.

Two front pads occupy the approved X=-4..0 ranges, the left fence occupies X=18..162,Y=-4..0,Z=0..12, and their connector remains at Y=-8..0 outside clamps.
One integral key tongue occupies X=0..3.8,Y=9.2..14.8,Z=-2.8..0 when seated, matching but not altering the supplied indexing notch with 0.20 mm in-plane clearance per side.
The jig is no more than 17.5 mm above the tube top and non-bushing material stays outside a 25 mm diameter vertical access cylinder at every drill axis.
The design guides 6.6 mm drilling through only the nominal 3 mm top wall and does not imply drilling or locating from the opposite wall.
A clear front arrow provides visual wrong-end confirmation in addition to the positive key.
The design note explicitly identifies machined acetal as the assumed digital-study material and does not imply production approval.
The output set contains a STEP or STL jig, hole-layout DXF, and machine-readable dimension/clearance report.
The result leaves supplier fit, evacuation, spindle clearance, runout, guarding, breakthrough, setup, and physical tolerance verification for later human review and makes no standards claim.

requirements.text: Every candidate is executed with the approved wright-water-heater-v1@0.1.0 recorded Modelica kit and its accepted parameter schema; an analytical or Python substitute is not labeled as kit execution.
Runs use 0.350 kg water, 4180 J/(kg·K), 90 J/K vessel capacity, 20 °C initial/ambient temperature, UA=0.60 W/K and electrical-to-thermal efficiency 0.92 without silent substitution.
sources: Supplied model quantities; Shared physical assumptions

requirements.text: Constant electrical power is applied until the first 90 °C target crossing using the selected kit's declared 2 K hysteresis semantics; post-crossing energy is not counted as heat-up energy.
The study retains actual results for all and only the declared P350, P500 and P700 electrical-power candidates.
Each baseline run uses the accepted 300 s horizon and 1 s output grid; the comparison records if a candidate does not reach 90 °C within that horizon.
Candidate compliance uses the independently interpolated first 90 °C crossing and the inclusive 180 s heat-up limit.
The recommendation selects the lowest declared electrical power that meets 180 s, or reports no feasible candidate without changing mass or the power menu.
The report separates electrical input energy, thermal energy delivered to water/vessel, and modeled ambient loss over the declared target-crossing horizon.
The selected controlling candidate retains a separate refined run using the authorized tighter timestep/tolerance and reports target-time and final-energy sensitivity.
sources: Physical and numerical contract; Real result export and study analysis

requirements.text: The output set contains temperature-time.csv, power-comparison.csv, energy-summary.csv, temperature curves, heater-selection report, and kit-parameters.json with kit/version, accepted names, run IDs and integration settings.

requirements.text: Every candidate is executed with the approved wright-water-heater-v1@0.1.0 recorded Modelica kit and accepted schema; analytical estimates remain separately labeled.
Runs use 0.600 kg water, 4180 J/(kg·K), 180 J/K vessel capacity, 20 °C initial/ambient temperature, UA=0.85 W/K and heater efficiency 0.93 without silent substitution.
Constant power is applied until the first 90 °C crossing using the selected kit's 2 K hysteresis semantics, and target-crossing energy uses that horizon.
The study retains actual results for P400, P600 and P800, with no candidate or recommendation above the 800 W continuous inverter limit.
Thermal compliance uses the independently interpolated first 90 °C crossing and the inclusive 360 s heat-up limit.
Battery-side energy equals heater AC electrical energy divided by 0.88, is labeled a postprocess estimate, states any standby-load exclusion, and is compared with the 70 Wh per-batch target.
The recommendation selects the lowest declared power meeting both 360 s thermal and 70 Wh battery-side targets without reducing batch mass or changing the power limit.

requirements.text: The pin schedule and harness preserve every declared J0/JF/JS pin and net; at B1 only +24V is spliced, while FAN_GND and SIGNAL_RETURN remain separate to the J0 controller star point.
Conductor and splice calculations use 0.35/0.70 A fan continuous/start current plus 0.03 A transmitter current, including 0.38/0.73 A on the shared supply trunk.
Every loaded branch remains at or below 0.72 V drop in separate continuous and startup cases using both supply and return segments at 35 °C, with contact resistance sourced or explicitly assumed.

The cut list derives each unique conductor from installed centerline routes, adds 50 mm service length at each connector termination plus documented strip/crimp allowance, and does not double-count the shared trunk.

Selected real connector housings, terminals and tools have sourced compatibility and ratings meeting each pin count, at least the declared current, 30 V and 35 °C; physical pin order is not inferred from logical IDs.
The plan maintains 25 mm minimum bend radius, 30 mm hot-wall clearance, an external bundle, and removable labels at J0, JF and JS.
The report retains the 22..26 V supply range, 2 A current limit and 3.3 V-compatible PWM/tach assumption while leaving actual fan-interface compatibility for sourced verification.
Every connector view is explicitly labeled mating-face or wire-entry and is consistent with the exact pin schedule without silent mirroring.
The output set contains a labeled harness plan, pin schedule, cut list, BOM, assembly instructions and voltage-drop results in the requested machine-readable/rendered formats.
The result does not claim a production-certified harness or perform energizing, machine modification, fabrication, or purchasing.
The harness preserves all declared pins/nets, separate +24V and POWER_GND splices at B0, continuous SIGNAL_RETURN to J0 pin 6, and a controller-only star-point connection.
Shared-trunk sizing uses simultaneous startup of both fans and transmitter: 4.025 A on +24V and 4.0 A on POWER_GND; each branch retains its declared continuous/start current.
Every loaded branch, including the farthest fan, remains at or below 0.72 V in separate continuous and simultaneous-start cases using both shared and branch supply/return paths at 45 °C.
The cut list uses each unique centerline route, 50 mm service length at each connector termination plus documented strip/crimp allowance, and never double-counts shared trunks.
Selected sourced connector/splice parts and tools meet declared pin counts, 30 V, 45 °C derating, at least 5 A at J0/B0, 3 A at fan connectors and 0.1 A at signal contacts.
sources: Assembly and procurement needs; Fabrication capability and policies

requirements.text: Fans unplug independently, the common trunk has abrasion sleeve and clips at no more than 300 mm spacing, and the harness remains at least 50 mm from irrigation tubing.
FAN_A_TACH, FAN_B_TACH, HUM_SIGNAL and SIGNAL_RETURN remain on their declared pins, and open-collector tach compatibility is recorded as an assumption requiring selection verification.
Connector views are explicitly mating-face or wire-entry and match the exact pin schedule without mirroring.
The output set contains harness plan, exact pin schedule, cut list, BOM, assembly instructions and voltage-drop evidence.
The result does not claim sealed certification or production qualification and does not perform live connection, fabrication, machine modification, or purchasing.

requirements.text: The harness preserves every declared J0/ZX/ZY/load pin and net; fan returns and each zone sensor return remain separate until the external controller star point.

requirements.text: Pin 6 at both ZX and ZY is explicitly marked reserve/unconnected and is not bonded to ground or any other net.
Each pressure signal/return uses a shielded twisted pair whose drain bonds only at the controller chassis termination and is neither a load return nor protective earth.
Shared segments use the summed simultaneous startup currents, including 3.28 A on common +24V, 3.20 A on common FAN_RETURN and 1.64 A per zone supply.

requirements.text: Every fan and sensor branch remains at or below 0.72 V in separate continuous and simultaneous-start cases using all shared/branch supply and return segments at 50 °C.
Each load-side +24V split uses a documented permissible two-conductor terminal or an explicit located splice; no unapproved double-crimp is assumed.
The cut list uses unique centerline routes, 50 mm connector service allowances plus documented strip/crimp allowance, and does not double-count shared trunks.
Selected sourced connector/terminal/tool combinations meet pin counts, 30 V, 50 °C derating, at least 4 A at J0, 2 A at ZX/ZY power contacts and 0.1 A at sensor contacts.
